clue.text: Get an alternative clergyman round, one for Brighton rally?

indicators.note: the clergyman's letters go round the rearranged piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a vicar is a parish clergyman

indicators.note: an alternative version of the words get an is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fetch another vicar for a rally in Brighton.
explanation.walkthrough: The London to Brighton run is a famous annual rally for veteran motor cars, so the definition points to an old automobile rather than a clergyman's outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Old motor cars from the early years of motoring take part in the London to Brighton run.

clue.text: State where one lake reflected no island

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals and L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: the pair is shown reflected, as in a mirror, so it appears beside itself in reverse order

parts.note: the same one and lake give I and L a second time, as their mirror image

explanation.surface: In one US state, a lake's mirror image shows no island at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' places IL beside its mirror image LI, giving ILLI, which is followed by NO and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Prize lifted -—- one having finished here?

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup or a jackpot

explanation.surface: A trophy is raised aloft by the winner as they finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses POT in this down entry. The definition is cryptic: whoever finishes at the top has won.
explanation.definitionFit: The winner of a race or league finishes in the top place.

clue.text: Good tip to gather

parts.note: to tip is to lean over

explanation.surface: A useful tip is worth picking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a noun, a piece of advice, but is the verb meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, like collecting leftover grain after harvest.

clue.text: Element with iodine in mud drifting into river

indicators.note: the combined piece goes into the river's name, splitting it

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

indicators.note: iodine goes inside the rearranged letters
drifting suggests the letters of mud wander out of their order

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemical element, iodine, is found in mud drifting downstream into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river through Cambridge; 'drifting' scrambles mud before the iodine goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadmium is a metallic chemical element, symbol Cd.

clue.text: With respect to team, fine to drop single place

parts.note: RE means with respect to, as in business letters
a side is a team

indicators.note: the single letter is dropped from the word for fine

parts.note: nice can mean fine, as in 'a nice distinction'
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Regarding a sports team, it's fine to leave one player out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' takes I out of NICE, leaving NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling place, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Mouth piece the wrong way round

indicators.note: reading the word for piece the wrong way round means taking its letters from the end backwards

parts.note: a part is a piece of something

explanation.surface: A mouthpiece, such as on a wind instrument, has been fitted back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' turns PART into its reverse. 'Mouth piece' looks like one word, mouthpiece, but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Hexed, almost broke, in game of poker

indicators.note: broke suggests the letters of hexed and almost are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gambler, jinxed and nearly penniless, is playing poker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like an instruction to shorten something, but it is part of the anagram fodder, which 'broke' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas hold 'em is the most popular variant of poker, with shared community cards.

clue.text: Bill carries pig on ship

indicators.note: the word for bill carries the pig inside it

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A man named Bill has a pig with him on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but means an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a ship, train or aircraft.

clue.text: Friend back inside a shed, perhaps one's unlocked?

indicators.note: the turned word for friend goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the letters of a shed may be rearranged into another order
back means the word for friend is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A pal is found inside a garden shed, which is perhaps left unlocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition puns on locks of hair: a bald man is without locks, so he is unlocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphead is British slang for a bald man, someone with no locks of hair.

clue.text: The other heavyweight church assistant

parts.note: 'a bit of the other' is British slang for sex, so 'the other' means sex
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Someone describes a large person who helps out at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is a coy British euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and churchyard and often digs graves.

clue.text: Togetherness evident, as son welcomed into marriage

indicators.note: the son is taken inside the word for marriage, as if welcomed in

parts.note: a marriage is a union
S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Family unity is plain when a son is welcomed into a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed into' puts S inside UNION, between its I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together, as one.

clue.text: Pudding identified, clever fellow!

parts.note: to have spotted something is to have identified it
a clever dick is a know-all, so dick is the fellow

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a pudding and is praised for being clever.
explanation.walkthrough: A clever dick is British slang for a smart alec. Spotted dick is a traditional British steamed suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a British steamed pudding studded with dried fruit.

clue.text: Business in tiny pieces, railway

parts.note: dust is made of tiny particles

explanation.surface: A company's business has been smashed to bits, railway included.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means commercial activity or a branch of trade, as does business.

clue.text: Rome rising after movement, to this?

definitions.text: Rome rising after movement, to this?

indicators.note: after its letters have been moved about, the phrase Rome rising gives a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rome, rising up after a political movement, led to what?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the history: the Risorgimento was the nineteenth-century movement that unified Italy, with Rome as its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Risorgimento was the movement for Italian unification, which made Rome the capital of the risen nation.

clue.text: Girl extremely passionate and alluring

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: amorous means passionate or full of love

explanation.surface: A girl is described as very passionate and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for passionate, but it takes the first and last letters of Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous means having alluring glamour and charm.

clue.text: Considerable time Northern Ireland's taken up, as necessary

indicators.note: in a down entry, taken up means the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: large means considerable in size
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A great deal of time in Northern Ireland has been spent, as was necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses the whole run LARGETNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means essential to completeness, so necessary.

clue.text: Exceptional answer by Conservative bound to divide church council

indicators.note: the inner pieces split the council's name into two parts

parts.note: the Council of Trent was a sixteenth-century church council
C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
a bound is a limit or end

explanation.surface: A remarkable reply from a Tory, sure to split a church council.
explanation.walkthrough: The Council of Trent (1545-63) is the church council most often meant in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Transcendent means surpassing ordinary limits, so exceptional or supreme.

clue.text: Look for sound doctrine in religion

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for look for is to be heard, giving a word that is spoken the same

parts.note: to look for is to seek
an ism is a doctrine or belief system

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a sound doctrine within religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, describing the doctrine, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhism is the monotheistic religion founded in the Punjab by Guru Nanak.

clue.text: Pub fighting to impress love — she's beautiful!

parts.note: PH, public house, is the abbreviation used on maps for a pub

indicators.note: the word for love is pressed into the word for fighting

parts.note: fighting is war
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: In a pub, a man fights to impress the woman he admires as beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to impress' puts O inside WAR. The answer is a British slang exclamation of lustful admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is British slang uttered on seeing someone attractive.

clue.text: Son takes fish and fruit

parts.note: a haddock is a fish

explanation.surface: A boy picks fish and fruit from the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is a large citrus fruit, the pomelo, named after a sea captain.

clue.text: One with temporary home more affected?

definitions.meaning: someone living in a tent or caravan on holiday
camp means theatrically affected, so this is its comparative form

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as the comparative of the adjective camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker in a tent has a temporary home, and camper also reads as 'more camp'.

clue.text: Fair to acquit

definitions.meaning: fair weather is fine and unclouded
to acquit someone is to declare them not guilty, freeing their name

explanation.definitionFit: Clear can mean fine and cloudless, like fair weather, and also means to declare innocent.

clue.text: Tile spotted on head of irate rocker's adversary, back to front

indicators.note: the whole run on, the first letter of irate and the mod is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Mods and Rockers were rival British youth gangs of the 1960s

explanation.surface: A tile is seen landing on the head of an angry rocker's rival, who is facing backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' turns ONIMOD into the answer. Mods (scooter riders) and Rockers (motorcyclists) were rival British youth gangs in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a small spotted tile used in a game.

clue.text: Green, turning ripe next

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of ripe next are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit that is green now turns ripe next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the colour of unripe fruit, but it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a common figurative word for inexperienced or lacking skill.

clue.text: Primate's head lowered, seeking vegetable

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering the head means moving the first letter to the bottom

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey bows its head, looking for vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head lowered' moves the A of APE from top to bottom in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a small round green vegetable.

clue.text: Weary, I must leave start of kilometre walk

indicators.note: the letter I is told to leave the word for weary

parts.note: to weary someone is to tire them

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tired walker feels unable to start the next kilometre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must leave' takes I out of TIRE, leaving TRE, and 'start of' gives the K of kilometre.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long walk or arduous journey on foot.

clue.text: Feat of acrobatics needing considerable attack, they say

indicators.note: they say means the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: some can mean considerable, as in 'that was some fight', and an assault is an attack

explanation.surface: An acrobatic stunt demands a lot of aggression, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: SOME ASSAULT, said quickly, sounds like the gymnastic flip.
explanation.definitionFit: A somersault is a flip in which the body turns heels over head, a classic acrobatic move.
